name: Traveling Salesman (DP)
description: Find the minimum-cost Hamiltonian cycle — visit every city exactly once and return to the start — using Held-Karp bitmask DP.
aim: Given n cities and pairwise travel costs, compute the shortest tour that visits every city exactly once and returns to the origin.
howItWorks: Represent visited-city subsets as bitmasks (2ⁿ possible subsets)
dp[mask][u] = minimum cost to reach city u having visited exactly the cities in mask
Base: dp[{0}][0] = 0 — start at city 0 with cost 0
Transition: for each mask and last city u, try extending to unvisited city v
After filling all dp states, find minimum dp[FULL][u] + dist[u][0] over all u
Backtrack through par[][] table to reconstruct the optimal route

time.bestCase: Held-Karp always runs in O(n²·2ⁿ) regardless of input
time.averageCase: Each of 2ⁿ subsets × n cities × n transitions
time.worstCase: Complete graph; practical limit is n ≈ 20

complexity.spaceDescription: DP table of size 2ⁿ × n storing minimum costs and parent pointers

realWorld: Logistics: optimizing delivery routes for couriers
PCB manufacturing: minimizing drill-head travel distance
Telescope scheduling: minimizing slew time between targets
Circuit board testing: efficient probe path planning
whenToUse: When n ≤ 20 and an exact optimal solution is required
When exponential time is acceptable (small instances)
When tour cost must be globally minimal, not approximate
When you need to reconstruct the full optimal path
alternatives: Nearest-neighbor heuristic O(n²): fast, ~25% above optimal
Christofides algorithm O(n³): guarantees within 1.5× optimal
Lin-Kernighan heuristic: high quality for large n
